name: Jeremiah
bio:
Jeremiah was a prophet of Judah. His first mention in Scripture comes at the death of King Josiah in 638 BC: when Josiah died at Megiddo, Jeremiah composed a lament for him that the singing men and women of Israel continued to sing in his memory, a tradition still kept at the time Chronicles was written (2 Chronicles 35:25). His own long and eventful ministry is told in detail in the book that bears his name. Chronicles closes the book of Kings' story by tying the exile directly to Jeremiah's prophetic word: the land's seventy years of desolation and sabbath rest fulfilled what the LORD had spoken through him, and it was likewise to fulfill his word that the LORD later stirred up Cyrus of Persia to let the exiles return (2 Chronicles 36:21-22).

## 📖 Core Story: Called from the Womb

Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest from Anathoth in Benjamin, received his call in the thirteenth year of King Josiah: the LORD told him he had been set apart as a prophet to the nations even before birth. Despite Jeremiah's protest that he was too young to speak, the LORD touched his mouth and commissioned him to pronounce judgment and restoration over kingdoms, promising to make him an iron pillar no enemy could overcome (Jeremiah 1:1-19).

## 📖 Core Story: Persecution Under Jehoiakim and Zedekiah

Jeremiah's ministry, spanning the reigns of Josiah, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah until Jerusalem's fall, brought him constant conflict. Pashur the priest once had him beaten and put in stocks for prophesying the city's destruction (Jeremiah 20:1-6). Preaching repentance at the temple early in Jehoiakim's reign, he was seized by priests and prophets who wanted him executed for predicting the temple's ruin; only the elders' memory of an earlier unpunished prophet, and the protection of Ahikam son of Shaphan, kept him alive — though another prophet, Urijah, was hunted down in Egypt and killed for saying the same things (Jeremiah 26:1-24). He wore a wooden yoke symbolizing Babylon's dominance until the false prophet Hananiah broke it and was condemned to die within the year, which he did (Jeremiah 27:1-28:17).

While imprisoned during the Babylonian siege, Jeremiah bought a field from his cousin Hanameel as a sign of future restoration, entrusting the deed to his scribe Baruch (Jeremiah 32:1-15). He used a visit from the ascetic Rechabite clan, who refused wine in obedience to their ancestor Jehonadab's generations-old command, as an object lesson in faithfulness that Judah itself had failed to keep (Jeremiah 35:1-19). Early in Jehoiakim's reign, Jeremiah dictated all his prophecies to Baruch on a scroll; after officials heard it read and warned the two men to hide, King Jehoiakim burned the scroll and ordered their arrest, but the LORD hid them and Jeremiah simply had Baruch rewrite it (Jeremiah 36:1-32). Under Zedekiah, officials repeatedly sent for his counsel yet resented his message of surrender as treasonous; they eventually threw him into a muddy cistern to die, from which Ebed-melech the Cushite rescued him with the king's permission (Jeremiah 37:1-38:28).

## 📖 Core Story: The Fall of Jerusalem and Exile to Egypt

When Jerusalem fell, Nebuchadnezzar ordered Jeremiah well treated; he chose to stay in Judah under the newly appointed governor Gedaliah rather than go to Babylon (Jeremiah 39:1-40:6). After Ishmael son of Nethaniah assassinated Gedaliah and Johanan son of Kareah rescued the survivors, the people asked Jeremiah to seek the LORD's guidance; he told them to remain in Judah rather than flee to Egypt, warning that Egypt itself would fall to Babylon, but the group distrusted him and went to Egypt anyway, taking Jeremiah and Baruch with them (Jeremiah 42:1-43:7). In Egypt, Jeremiah confronted the refugees for continuing to worship idols and prophesied that Nebuchadnezzar would conquer Egypt too, with Pharaoh Hophra's death as a sign (Jeremiah 43:8-44:30). He also sent a short word of comfort to the anxious Baruch, promising his life would be spared amid the coming disaster, wherever he went (Jeremiah 45:1-5). Some speculated Jesus might be Jeremiah or one of the other ancient prophets (Matthew 16:14).
